name: swe-search-lsp-bridge
description: Local, offline semantic code search with no LLM: a Search by meaning / Find similar UI plus an LSP symbol bridge for the semantic search MCP server. Local-only named pipe, no network access, no runtime dependencies beyond VS Code itself.

chatParticipants.name: codebase
chatParticipants.description: Ask about this workspace using the local, offline Foundry index — no cloud indexing.

commands.name: index
commands.description: Show what the local index covers (repo overview)

commands.name: graph
commands.description: Render a Mermaid call graph for a symbol (prefix 'callers' to invert)

languageModelTools.name: foundry_semanticSearch
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search THIS workspace's code by meaning using the local, offline Foundry index. Returns ranked symbols with file:line ranges and one-line signatures. Prefer this over reading files to locate where functionality lives. Pass expand with result numbers to fetch full bodies of specific hits. Multi-word queries mixing a likely identifier with a common word (e.g. "xyz block") are handled internally — compound/proximity matching plus an auto-complement to symbol lookup keep a rare identifier from being drowned out by the common word's other uses; you don't need to query the parts separately.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search your codebase by meaning using the local Foundry index.

query.description: Natural-language or code query describing what to find.

expand.description: Result numbers from a prior search to fetch full code for.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_searchSymbol
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Look up a symbol by exact or partial name in this workspace (functions, classes, methods, and non-callable declarations like interfaces/enums/types). Use when you know the identifier name. foundry_semanticSearch already auto-probes this same index for compound-identifier candidates in multi-word queries, so the two complement each other automatically — call this directly only when you already have a specific name to check.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_traceCalls
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show the direct callers and callees of a symbol (one level) from this workspace's call graph. Provide the file and definition line from a prior search result; include the symbol name for the offline fallback.

file.description: Absolute file path of the symbol.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_showExecutionFlow
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Walk the call graph several levels deep from a symbol in one call — downstream callees or upstream callers — returning an indented tree. Use to trace a whole flow (e.g. 'what does checkout eventually call').

file.description: Absolute file path of the symbol.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_findUsages
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List every reference to a symbol across this workspace — use for 'where is X used?' and impact analysis before a change. Provide the file and definition line; include the symbol name for the offline fallback.

file.description: Absolute file path of the symbol.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_findImplementations
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find the concrete implementations of an interface or abstract member in this workspace. Provide the file and definition line; include the symbol name for the offline fallback.

file.description: Absolute file path of the symbol.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_architectureOverview
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get a module-level architecture map of this workspace (modules = directories with their dependencies, dependents, entry points, and reference hotspots). Pass module to drill into one directory. Use to understand how the codebase is organized.

module.description: Optional directory path, file path, or name to drill into.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_repoOverview
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get a quick orientation summary of the indexed workspace: file/chunk counts, language breakdown, and which code-intelligence indexes (symbols, call graph, usages, implementations) are built.

languageModelTools.name: foundry_readFile
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read a workspace file, two-pass to stay token-lean. Call with just `file` to get an OUTLINE first (the file's functions/classes/methods with line ranges, no bodies); then call again with `symbol="name"` to read just that symbol's code, or `startLine`/`endLine` for a range. Small files return whole. Use to read the EXACT file/module located via search_symbol, architecture_overview, or a semantic_search hit — real source, not fuzzy snippets. Absolute or workspace-relative path.

file.description: File to read — absolute or workspace-relative (e.g. "src/storage/store.ts").

symbol.description: Pass 2: read just this symbol's body (a name from the pass-1 outline).

outline.description: Force outline-only (symbols + line ranges, no bodies).

startLine.description: 1-based first line to read (a specific slice).

languageModelTools.name: foundry_listDirectory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the workspace directory STRUCTURE recursively — a file/folder tree that respects .gitignore/.sweignore (no node_modules/.git noise). Use to orient on an unfamiliar repo, see its layout, or find where files/dirs live (covers unindexed files too). Call with no path for the repo root; it is depth-limited, so drill into a branch by calling again with path="<subdir>" and/or a larger depth. Folders cut off by the depth limit are marked "/…".

path.description: Directory to list — absolute or workspace-relative. Omit for the repo root.

depth.description: How many levels deep to walk (default 3, max 10).

languageModelTools.name: foundry_projectStandards
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Report the project's detected standards: framework(s) (auto-detected, e.g. Drupal/Symfony/Laravel), the PSR-4 namespace→directory map, and the enforced coding standard — read from the ecosystem's own files (Composer's generated vendor artifacts, composer.json, a framework-specific marker like Drupal's *.info.yml when present, .foundry/standards.json), not guessed. Use on a PHP/Composer repo to learn how namespaces map to folders (foundry_readFile also accepts a fully-qualified class name and resolves it). Deterministic, offline, no index.

namespaces.description: Include the full PSR-4 map (default true).

languageModelTools.name: foundry_searchConfig
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the project's structured CONFIG (YAML), auto-detected and generic by default, with richer facts when a framework-specific pack matches (e.g. Drupal's config/sync views/fields/displays, *.services.yml / *.routing.yml / *.permissions.yml / *.info.yml) — plus any other .yml regardless. Config is NEVER embedded, so it is NOT in foundry_semanticSearch — this is how you reach it. Use for questions like 'which view lists published articles', 'what fields does the Article type have', 'what handles the /market/activity route', 'what does the market module depend on'. Returns items ranked exact-id > id/label > keyword, each with id, type, file:line and a facts summary (open the file with foundry_readFile for the raw YAML). Optionally filter by type (view, field, service, route, permission, module_info, …). Offline; needs the config index built.

query.description: Config id, label, or keywords, e.g. "frontpage", "article body", "activity route".

type.description: Optional: restrict to one config type, e.g. "view", "field", "service", "route", "permission".

languageModelTools.name: foundry_plan
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Produce a grounded implementation plan for a described change using the local Foundry index. Returns a DETERMINISTIC context pack — index/architecture overview, the most relevant code with FULL bodies, the project's own docs, relevant structured config, call-sites/usages of the key symbols (downstream impact), and the real build/test manifests — followed by a plan template to fill in. Use this when you need to plan HOW to implement a change (scope, files to touch, steps, risks, verify commands) grounded in this workspace, e.g. after taking over a task in agent mode. It does not edit files or run commands. Offline; needs the local index built.

request.description: The change to plan, in plain language, e.g. "add a retry with backoff to the fetch path" or "add a new field to the Article content type".

sweSearch.serverEntry.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the built MCP server entry, e.g. `/path/to/local-semantic-search-mcp/dist/index.js`. Required for the **Search by meaning** and **Find similar** commands.

sweSearch.nodePath.description: Path to the Node.js executable used to run the search server. Set an absolute path if VS Code can't find node (common with nvm), e.g. /home/you/.nvm/versions/node/vXX/bin/node.

sweSearch.topK.description: How many results each search returns.

sweSearch.showUsage.description: Show an estimated usage footer (model request count + approximate input/output tokens) under @codebase chat answers. This is a local estimate — VS Code does not expose exact Copilot credit/premium-request cost to extensions.
